findings.body:
**Fix the stale `maxUsd` doc. It contradicts the governor contract.**

The comment at src/kernel/types.ts:119 says `maxUsd` is "advisory here: USD is derived, callers govern". That statement is wrong in three ways:
- The governor enforces USD admission caps before dispatch. The path instructions say "admission caps (attempts, dispatch quota, USD/token rollups) reject before dispatch".
- "unpriced usage under a configured maxUsd trips loud", so the governor enforces this cap and does not treat it as advisory.
- The kernel does not derive USD. "USD is observed via reportUsage/reportCost, never derived by the kernel".

The sibling `maxTokens` doc at src/kernel/types.ts:121-125 already says "enforced by the governor". This file is the single source of truth for the frozen contract. A caller who reads the `maxUsd` doc can conclude that the cap is not enforced. The same "derived" wording appears at src/kernel/types.ts:146 (`JobOutcome.costUSD`) and src/kernel/types.ts:163. Align those docs with the observed-cost rule.

<details>
<summary>📝 Proposed doc fix</summary>

```diff
-  /** Run-level USD cap (advisory here: USD is derived, callers govern). */
+  /** Run-level USD cap: enforced by the governor against observed cost
+   * (reportUsage/reportCost; the kernel never derives USD). Unpriced usage
+   * under a configured cap trips the run. */
   maxUsd?: number;
```
</details>

As per path instructions: "USD is observed via reportUsage/reportCost, never derived by the kernel, and unpriced usage under a configured maxUsd trips loud".
findings.title: Fix the stale `maxUsd` doc. It contradicts the governor contract.
